q: In 1896, _____ discovered that uranium salts emit radiations which affect photographic plates and cause ionization.
e: In 1896, Henry Becquerel discovered that uranium salts emit radiations which affect photographic plates and cause ionization. Marie Curie and Albert Einstein belong to other processes, not this Henry Becquerel case. Becquerel saw uranium salts fog plates and ionize air in 1896.

q: The emission of some or all of alpha, beta and gamma rays from the nucleus of an unstable atom is called _____.
e: The emission of some or all of alpha, beta and gamma rays from the nucleus of an unstable atom is called radioactivity. nuclear fission and ionization belong to other processes, not this radioactivity case. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: The term radioactivity is also known as radioactive decay, radioactive disintegration, nuclear decay, or _____.
e: The term radioactivity is also known as radioactive decay, radioactive disintegration, nuclear decay, or nuclear disintegration. chemical decay and nuclear fission belong to other processes, not this nuclear disintegration case. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: The radiations are emitted from the nucleus of uranium atoms and are of three types; namely _____.
e: The radiations are emitted from the nucleus of uranium atoms and are of three types; namely alpha, beta and gamma rays. protons, neutrons and electrons and X-rays, UV and IR belong to other processes, not this alpha, beta and gamma rays case. Alpha decay throws out a helium nucleus, so A drops by 4 and Z by 2. Gamma decay dumps excitation energy as a photon; Z and A stay put.

q: Of all 92 elements which exist in nature, only a few heavy elements with atomic number greater than _____ are radioactive or unstable.
e: Of all 92 elements which exist in nature, only a few heavy elements with atomic number greater than 83 are radioactive or unstable. Put 92 or 100 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: Some examples of radioactive elements are uranium, thorium, radium, polonium and radon; of which radium and polonium were discovered by _____.
e: Some examples of radioactive elements are uranium, thorium, radium, polonium and radon; of which radium and polonium were discovered by Marie Curie. Henry Becquerel and Willard Libby belong to other processes, not this Marie Curie case. The Curies isolated radium and polonium from pitchblende and named radioactivity. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: Radioactive elements can also be artificially produced using nuclear reactors and _____.
e: Radioactive elements can also be artificially produced using nuclear reactors and particle accelerators. Put mass spectrometers or cyclotrons only in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma. A reactor is a vessel where a fission chain can be started, held, and steered.

q: Alpha decay ($\alpha$ decay) is a process in which an atomic nucleus emits an alpha particle and transforms into a different atomic nucleus, with mass number reduces by four and atomic number reduces by _____.
e: Alpha decay (alpha decay) is a process in which an atomic nucleus emits an alpha particle and transforms into a different atomic nucleus, with mass number reduces by four and atomic number reduces by two. one is not two, and four is not two either. Alpha decay throws out a helium nucleus, so A drops by 4 and Z by 2. Nuclear changes happen in the nucleus, not in the electron cloud of chemistry.

q: In $\beta^-$ decay, a neutron in an atomic nucleus changes to a proton with the emission of an electron and an _____.
e: In beta^- decay, a neutron in an atomic nucleus changes to a proton with the emission of an electron and an antineutrino. neutrino is not antineutrino, and positron is not antineutrino either. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus.

q: In $\beta^+$ decay, a proton in an atomic nucleus changes to a neutron with the emission of a positron and a _____.
e: In beta^+ decay, a proton in an atomic nucleus changes to a neutron with the emission of a positron and a neutrino. Put photon or antineutrino in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A proton is a positive nucleon; beta-plus decay turns a proton into a neutron. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus.

q: Positron, the antiparticle of electron, has the same mass and same magnitude of electric charge as an electron; but positron is _____ charged.
e: Positron, the antiparticle of electron, has the same mass and same magnitude of electric charge as an electron; but positron is positively charged. negatively is not positively, and neutrally is not positively either. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: The existence of positron was theoretically predicted by Dirac in 1931 and experimentally detected by _____ in 1932.
e: The existence of positron was theoretically predicted by Dirac in 1931 and experimentally detected by Anderson in 1932. Put Thomson or Rutherford in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Beta-plus turns a proton into a neutron, a positron, and a neutrino.

q: Neutrino, a fundamental particle as an electron, has no charge and negligibly small rest mass which is less than _____ kg.
e: Neutrino, a fundamental particle as an electron, has no charge and negligibly small rest mass which is less than 2 × 10^-37 kg. Put 9. 1 × 10^-31 or 1. 6 × 10^-19 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics.

q: If a nucleus has excess neutrons, _____ decay takes place.
e: If a nucleus has excess neutrons, beta^- decay takes place. beta^+ and alpha belong to other processes, not this beta^- case. Nuclear changes happen in the nucleus, not in the electron cloud of chemistry.

q: Conversely, a nucleus with excess protons undergoes _____ decay.
e: Conversely, a nucleus with excess protons undergoes beta^+ decay. Put γ or beta^- in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A proton is a positive nucleon; beta-plus decay turns a proton into a neutron. Nuclear changes happen in the nucleus, not in the electron cloud of chemistry.

q: In gamma decay, the atomic number and mass number of the parent and daughter nuclei remain _____.
e: In gamma decay, the atomic number and mass number of the parent and daughter nuclei remain unchanged. increased is not unchanged, and decreased is not unchanged either. Nuclear changes happen in the nucleus, not in the electron cloud of chemistry. Gamma decay dumps excitation energy as a photon; Z and A stay put.

q: The photon is the quantum of the electromagnetic field and photons are massless and move at the speed of light in _____.
e: The photon is the quantum of the electromagnetic field and photons are massless and move at the speed of light in vacuum. Put air or water in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Einstein's 1905 photon is the particle side of light, energy hf.

q: The energy of a photon is inversely proportional to the _____ of the electromagnetic radiation associated with it.
e: The energy of a photon is inversely proportional to the wavelength of the electromagnetic radiation associated with it. Put frequency or amplitude in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Einstein's 1905 photon is the particle side of light, energy hf.

q: Alpha rays consist of helium nuclei, positively charged particles, and the charge of an $\alpha$ particle is _____.
e: Alpha rays consist of helium nuclei, positively charged particles, and the charge of an alpha particle is +2e. Put -e or +e in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Nuclear changes happen in the nucleus, not in the electron cloud of chemistry. Alpha decay throws out a helium nucleus, so A drops by 4 and Z by 2.

q: Alpha rays are the _____ ionizing of the three rays.
e: Alpha rays are the most ionizing of the three rays. Put least or moderately in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Alpha decay throws out a helium nucleus, so A drops by 4 and Z by 2.

q: Alpha rays are the least penetrating of the three rays and can be stopped by a thick sheet of _____.
e: Alpha rays are the least penetrating of the three rays and can be stopped by a thick sheet of paper. Put lead or aluminium in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Alpha decay throws out a helium nucleus, so A drops by 4 and Z by 2.

q: Beta rays can be stopped by a few millimetres of _____.
e: Beta rays can be stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium. Put paper or lead in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Beta rays can be stopped by a few millimetres of _____. aluminium.

q: Gamma rays are electromagnetic waves like light and X-rays, but have much shorter wavelengths and are high energy _____.
e: Gamma rays are electromagnetic waves like light and X-rays, but have much shorter wavelengths and are high energy photons. Put electrons or protons in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Gamma decay dumps excitation energy as a photon; Z and A stay put. Einstein's 1905 photon is the particle side of light, energy hf.

q: Gamma rays cannot be deflected by _____ fields.
e: Gamma rays cannot be deflected by electric and magnetic fields. Put gravitational only or nuclear in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Gamma decay dumps excitation energy as a photon; Z and A stay put.

q: Intensity of gamma rays can be greatly reduced by several centimetres of _____ but they are never completely stopped.
e: Intensity of gamma rays can be greatly reduced by several centimetres of lead but they are never completely stopped. Put paper or aluminium in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Gamma decay dumps excitation energy as a photon; Z and A stay put.

q: The rate of decay of a radioactive sample is called _____ and its SI unit is becquerel (Bq).
e: The rate of decay of a radioactive sample is called activity and its SI unit is becquerel (Bq). half-life is not activity, and mass defect is not activity either. Becquerel saw uranium salts fog plates and ionize air in 1896. Activity is decays per second, the rate at which particles or gamma rays leave the sample.

q: Units larger than Bq are MBq ($10^6$ Bq) and _____ ($10^9$ Bq).
e: Units larger than Bq are MBq (10^6 Bq) and GBq (10^9 Bq). kBq is not GBq, and TBq is not GBq either. The power 10^6 is the conversion for this unit; a nearby prefix is a different size.

q: 1 curie (Ci) is equal to _____ event $s^{-1}$.
e: 1 curie (Ci) is equal to 3. 7 × 10^10 event s^-1. Put 3. 7 × 10^8 or 1.

q: The rate of decay (activity) is a characteristic of the radioactive element and it is unaffected by the _____.
e: The rate of decay (activity) is a characteristic of the radioactive element and it is unaffected by the temperature. pressure is not temperature, and magnetic field is not temperature either. Activity is decays per second, the rate at which particles or gamma rays leave the sample. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: The half-life is defined as the time for _____ the atoms in a radioactive sample to decay.
e: The half-life is defined as the time for half the atoms in a radioactive sample to decay. Put all or one-fourth in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Half-life is the time for half the nuclei in the sample to decay; activity halves on the same clock. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: Half-life of radioactive substances ranges from about femtosecond to billions of years, where femtosecond is _____ s.
e: Half-life of radioactive substances ranges from about femtosecond to billions of years, where femtosecond is 10^-15 s. Put 10^-12 or 10^-9 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: Radioactive decay is a statistical process and the decay rate can be expressed as a decay constant or as half-life, leading to the _____ law of radioactive decay.
e: Radioactive decay is a statistical process and the decay rate can be expressed as a decay constant or as half-life, leading to the exponential law of radioactive decay. linear is not exponential, and inverse is not exponential either. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma. Half-life is the time for half the nuclei in the sample to decay; activity halves on the same clock.

q: A small amount of radioactive isotope introduced into a system in order to follow the behaviour of some components of that system is called a _____.
e: A small amount of radioactive isotope introduced into a system in order to follow the behaviour of some components of that system is called a tracer. moderator and coolant belong to other processes, not this tracer case. A tracer is a tiny radioisotope dose you follow through a body, pipe, or plant.

q: In medicine, to check thyroid function, the patient drinks an iodine solution containing a small amount of radioactive _____.
e: In medicine, to check thyroid function, the patient drinks an iodine solution containing a small amount of radioactive iodine-131. cobalt-60 and carbon-14 belong to other processes, not this iodine-131 case. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: In industry, small amounts of radioactive substances are added as tracers to materials in various processes to monitor fluid flow, detect leaks, and to study the rate of wear, erosion and _____ of equipment.
e: In industry, small amounts of radioactive substances are added as tracers to materials in various processes to monitor fluid flow, detect leaks, and to study the rate of wear, erosion and corrosion of equipment. melting is not corrosion, and freezing is not corrosion either. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: In agriculture, fertilizers labelled with radioactive isotopes phosphorus-32 and _____ have been used to study the uptake of fertilizers.
e: In agriculture, fertilizers labelled with radioactive isotopes phosphorus-32 and nitrogen-15 have been used to study the uptake of fertilizers. carbon-14 is not nitrogen-15, and uranium-235 is not nitrogen-15 either. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: Treatment with radiation is known as _____ and radioisotopes such as cobalt-60 are widely used to treat cancer.
e: Treatment with radiation is known as radiotherapy and radioisotopes such as cobalt-60 are widely used to treat cancer. Put radiography or irradiation in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A radioisotope is an unstable nuclide that decays and emits radiation. Radiotherapy aims ionizing beams at tissue to kill or shrink diseased cells.

q: In industrial gamma radiography, radioactive materials are used to inspect metal castings or _____ joints.
e: In industrial gamma radiography, radioactive materials are used to inspect metal castings or welded joints. broken is not welded, and glued is not welded either. Gamma decay dumps excitation energy as a photon; Z and A stay put. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: In a thickness monitoring system, if the cord from the rollers becomes too thin, _____ beta radiation reaches the detector.
e: In a thickness monitoring system, if the cord from the rollers becomes too thin, more beta radiation reaches the detector. Put less or no in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The rollers becomes too thin, _____ beta radiation reaches the detector. more.

q: Radioactive dating is a technique for estimating the age of an object by measuring the amounts of various _____ present in it.
e: Radioactive dating is a technique for estimating the age of an object by measuring the amounts of various radioisotopes present in it. Put stable isotopes or molecules in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Radioactive dating compares residual radioisotopes to clock the age of rock or remains.

q: Carbon dating is a technique, developed by _____, for estimating the age of the remains of plants and animals.
e: Carbon dating is a technique, developed by Willard Libby, for estimating the age of the remains of plants and animals. Marie Curie and Albert Einstein belong to other processes, not this Willard Libby case. Carbon dating reads leftover carbon-14 activity in once-living remains.

q: The half-life of carbon-14 is _____ years.
e: The half-life of carbon-14 is 5730 years. Put 1620 or 1300 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Carbon dating reads leftover carbon-14 activity in once-living remains. Half-life is the time for half the nuclei in the sample to decay; activity halves on the same clock.

q: There is one carbon-14 atom in every _____ of carbon-12 atoms in the atmosphere.
e: There is one carbon-14 atom in every trillion of carbon-12 atoms in the atmosphere. Put billion or million in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Carbon dating reads leftover carbon-14 activity in once-living remains.

q: The age of igneous rocks can be estimated by the proportion of potassium-40 to its stable decay product, _____.
e: The age of igneous rocks can be estimated by the proportion of potassium-40 to its stable decay product, argon-40. Put lead or carbon-12 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. By the proportion of potassium-40 to its stable decay product, _____. argon-40.

q: Lead is the stable final decay product of a series of decays that starts with _____.
e: Lead is the stable final decay product of a series of decays that starts with uranium. Put potassium or carbon in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: Gamma and neutron irradiation of seeds can be used to induce mutations to develop desired mutants that are resistant to _____.
e: Gamma and neutron irradiation of seeds can be used to induce mutations to develop desired mutants that are resistant to disease. drought is not disease, and radiation is not disease either. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus. Gamma decay dumps excitation energy as a photon; Z and A stay put.

q: Irradiation of food has potential to produce safe foods with long _____.
e: Irradiation of food has potential to produce safe foods with long shelf life. half-life is not shelf life, and decay rate is not shelf life either. Irradiation of food has potential to produce safe foods with long _____. shelf life.
